q-183452.name: Question 1
q-183452.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ For all $t\in Q,$ $t<1.$
q-183452.worked_solution:
If we denote

$$
P(t):t<1,
$$

our statement can be written as

$$
∀t\in Q,\,P(t).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
¬(∀t\in Q,\,P(t))≡∃t\in Q,\,¬P(t).
$$

Finally, $∃t\in Q,\,¬P(t)$ reads as follows:

$\,$ **There exists** $t\in Q$ such that $t\ge 1.$

q-183652.name: Question 2
q-183652.problem:
Negate the following statement: 

$\,$ Some composite numbers are not divisible by $3.$
q-183652.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be the set of all composite numbers. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ There exists $x\in C$ such that $x$ is not divisible by $3.$

Introducing the existential quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∃x\in C,\,x\text{ is not divisible by }3.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃x\in C,\,x\text{ is not divisible by }3) & ≡∀x\in C,\,¬(x\text{ is not divisible by }3) \\  & ≡∀x\in C,\,x\text{ is divisible by }3\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ For all $x\in C,$ $x\text{ is divisible by }3.$

or simply

$\,$ All composite numbers are divisible by $3.$

q-216595.name: Question 4
q-216595.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ Every universal statement is not true.
q-216595.worked_solution:
Let $U$ be the set of all universal statements. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ For all $x\in U,$ $x$ is not true.

Introducing the universal quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∀x\in U,\,x\text{ is not true}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀x\in U,\,x\text{ is not true}) & ≡∃x\in U,\,¬(x\text{ is not true}) \\  & ≡∃x\in U,\,x\text{ is true}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ There exists $x\in U$ such that $x$ is true.

or simply

$\,$ Some universal statements are true.
